waves.title: What a corporate travel policy should actually say
waves.keywords: corporate travel policy, business travel policy UK, travel policy template, what to include in a travel policy, travel and expense policy
waves.brief:
Reader: a travel manager, office manager, HR lead or finance director at a 40 to 400 person UK employer with no travel team, told to write or rewrite the travel policy. The decision is what each clause says and who signs it off.

What ranks and why it fails: page one is TMC and software marketing. TravelPerk (travelperk.com, perk.com), Corporate Traveller (corptraveller.com), Booking.com for Business and Meon Valley Travel all rank with gated template downloads, SERP checked 17 November 2026. Each assumes you book through the publisher. None gives the tax consequence of a clause and none cites HMRC.

Structure: the six decisions to take first (who approves, advance booking window, cabin caps, hotel ceiling by city, what happens on a breach, who answers at 2am). Then one section per clause: the clause, the decision behind it, the tax or legal consequence, one line of suggested wording.

Source anchors, checked live 17 November 2026. HMRC manual EIM30240 sets the tax free benchmark meal rates under the Income Tax (Approved Expenses) Regulations 2015: 5 pounds for qualifying travel of 5 hours or more, 10 pounds at 10 hours or more, 25 pounds at 15 hours or more and ongoing at 8pm, plus a 10 pound supplement where a 5 or 10 pound journey runs past 8pm; updated 3 November 2026. HMRC page EIM05231 still shows 5, 5, 10 and 15 pound rates but says they applied only from 6 April 2009 to 5 April 2016, which is where stale vendor blogs get their figures. For the cabin clause, gov.uk Air Passenger Duty rates show that from 1 April 2026 Band A is 15 pounds reduced against 32 pounds standard, and Band B 102 pounds against 244 pounds, so permitting premium cabins more than doubles duty on short haul.

Structural requirements: the exact phrase corporate travel policy in the first paragraph. The clause walkthrough must be a table, columns Clause, The decision behind it, Tax or legal consequence. Link out to gov.uk EIM30240, the gov.uk Air Passenger Duty rates page and gov.uk Expenses and benefits: travel. No gated template.

Scope limit: business travel as a company expense and a management problem only. No holidays, destinations, leisure agency or tour operator content. The reader is spending their employer's money. Never give legal or tax advice in our own voice: attribute every rule to HMRC or the named regulator and send the reader there.

waves.title: Duty of care: what employers owe business travellers
waves.keywords: duty of care business travel, employer duty of care travelling employees, travel risk management UK, travel risk assessment, lone worker business travel
waves.brief:
Reader: an HR or operations director, or a travel manager, asked, usually after a near miss or an insurer's question, what the company must do for staff it sends abroad. The decision is how much travel risk management to buy and what to put in writing.

What ranks and why it fails: International SOS, World Travel Protection, Riskline, TravelPerk and SAP Concur all publish explainers that name no statute, then pitch a product, and several conflate duty of care with travel insurance. Most are US or pan-EU in framing, and none walks a UK reader through the risk assessment they must already hold.

Structure: what the law says, what it means for one trip, the five artefacts a company should be able to produce (travel risk assessment, itinerary record, 24 hour contact route, pre-trip briefing, post-incident process).

Source anchors, checked live 17 November 2026. Section 2(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 puts a duty on every employer to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare at work of all his employees. Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999 regulation 3(1) requires a suitable and sufficient assessment of the risks; regulation 3(6) requires the significant findings in writing where the employer has five or more employees. HSE lone working guidance states that you must manage any health and safety risks before people can work alone. World Travel Protection research by Opinium among 500 UK business travellers, fieldwork 3 to 10 February 2025: 60 per cent said their employer could do more on their safety, and only 30 per cent of those with any support had a 24 hour emergency helpline.

Structural requirements: the exact phrase duty of care for business travellers in the first paragraph. The five artefacts must be a table, columns Artefact, What it must contain, Who owns it. Link out to legislation.gov.uk for HSWA 1974 section 2 and MHSWR 1999 regulation 3, HSE lone working, and FCDO travel advice on gov.uk.

Scope limit: business travel as a company expense and a management problem. No holidays, destinations or leisure content. Never state the law as advice in our own voice, never say whether a reader is compliant, never characterise criminal exposure: attribute every duty to the Act, the Regulations or HSE by name and send the reader to HSE or a solicitor.

waves.title: HMRC travel and subsistence: the employer rules
waves.keywords: HMRC travel and subsistence, benchmark scale rates, business travel expenses HMRC, travel benefit in kind, temporary workplace 24 month rule, P11D travel expenses
waves.brief:
Reader: a finance director, controller or payroll manager signing off travel claims. The decision is what can be reimbursed without a tax charge, what must be reported, and what rate to write into policy.

What ranks and why it fails: page one is expense software and contractor accountants. ExpenseIn, Wallester, ContractorCalculator and a stack of accountancy blogs rank, and the serious recurring error is publishing the 5, 5, 10 and 15 pound table as current. That table sits on HMRC page EIM05231, which says it applied from 6 April 2009 to 5 April 2016 only. Policy written from those blogs uses rates HMRC retired a decade ago.

Structure: the two questions HMRC asks (is it business travel, is the workplace temporary), the current rates, what must be reported, then the four traps.

Source anchors, checked live 17 November 2026. HMRC EIM30240 gives the current rates under the Income Tax (Approved Expenses) Regulations 2015: 5 pounds at 5 hours or more, 10 pounds at 10 hours or more, 25 pounds at 15 hours or more and ongoing at 8pm, plus a 10 pound late supplement. Conditions: absence from the normal workplace or home for more than five or ten continuous hours, a cost actually incurred on food and drink, evidence kept. Updated 3 November 2026. HMRC EIM32080, also updated 3 November 2026, sets the 24 month rule under sections 339(5) and (6) ITEPA 2003: a workplace is not temporary where attended during a period of continuous work lasting, or likely to last, more than 24 months, with a 40 per cent of working time test. Gov.uk Expenses and benefits: travel lists the narrow exemptions (works bus, taxi home after occasional and irregular late night working, cycles) and says travel and subsistence given through salary sacrifice must be reported.

Structural requirements: the exact phrase HMRC travel and subsistence in the first paragraph. Two tables: current rates (Qualifying travel, Maximum tax free amount, Conditions), and the retired 2009 to 2016 rates beside the current ones so the stale figures are visibly dated. Link out to gov.uk EIM30240, EIM32080 and Expenses and benefits: travel.

Scope limit: business travel as a company expense and a management problem. No holidays, destinations or leisure trade content. Never give tax advice in our own voice and never quote a rate without naming the HMRC page and its update date: send the reader to HMRC and their accountant.

waves.title: How to cut travel spend without banning travel
waves.keywords: cut business travel spend, reduce business travel costs, business travel cost savings, advance booking policy savings, rail vs air business travel cost
waves.brief:
Reader: a finance director or procurement lead given a budget cut, and the travel manager who must deliver it without a ban that pushes staff off policy. The decision is which lever to pull first, so order them by size of saving, not by ease of announcement.

What ranks and why it fails: TMC and expense platform marketing. TravelPerk, Navan, SAP Concur, Amex GBT and Corporate Traveller all rank with cost saving listicles, SERP checked 17 November 2026. Every list puts consolidate your bookings onto one platform at the top, because the publisher sells the platform. The reader cannot tell if a lever is worth 2 or 20 per cent.

Structure: levers in descending order of saving, with mechanism, example and who must agree. Test: cabin policy, advance booking windows, rail substitution on domestic and near-Europe routes, approval at request not at claim, hotel ceilings per city, consolidation last.

Source anchors, checked live 17 November 2026. Gov.uk Air Passenger Duty rates: from 1 April 2026 the standard rate is more than double the reduced rate on short haul (Band A, 32 against 15 pounds) and 244 against 102 pounds on Band B long haul. The Department for Transport announced on 2 March 2026 that regulated rail fares in England are frozen, saving passengers an expected 600 million pounds in 2026/27, against the 5.8 per cent rise (RPI plus one point) that would otherwise have applied. The GBTA Global Business Travel Forecast update with ALTOUR has global blended airfare up 4.7 per cent in 2026 to 756 dollars, economy up 8.7 per cent to 536 dollars and hotel average daily rate up 3.7 per cent to 168 dollars. An earlier CWT and GBTA 2026 forecast carried lower figures, so confirm on gbta.org which edition is current.

Structural requirements: use the exact phrase cut business travel spend in the first paragraph. The levers must be a table: Lever, Typical saving, Mechanism, Who has to agree. Link out to the gov.uk Air Passenger Duty rates page, the DfT fares freeze announcement and gbta.org. Any percentage not from a named source is a worked example, never a finding.

Scope limit: business travel as a company expense and a management problem. No holidays, destinations or leisure trade content. Never give tax or legal advice in our own voice: attribute any tax consequence to the named HMRC page and send the reader there.
